coverage.evidence: The source-verified two-manifold model assigns 18 electrons to each C18 π system; both satisfy 4k+2. The theorem proves aromaticCount .c18 = 2 by kernel-checked computation.
Neither 18-electron manifold satisfies the positive-4k predicate. The theorem proves antiaromaticCount .c18 = 0.
Both neutral ground-state C16 manifolds contain 16 electrons, so neither satisfies 4k+2. The theorem proves aromaticCount .c16 = 0.
Each of the two 16-electron C16 manifolds satisfies positive 4k. The theorem proves antiaromaticCount .c16 = 2.
The triplet configuration has 13 electrons in each π system; 13 is not 4k+2. The theorem proves aromaticCount .tripletC13 = 0.
Neither 13-electron triplet manifold is a positive multiple of four. The theorem proves antiaromaticCount .tripletC13 = 0.
The closed-shell singlet configuration distributes 14 and 12 electrons between the two manifolds; exactly the 14-electron system satisfies 4k+2. The theorem proves aromaticCount .singletC13 = 1.
Of the singlet populations 14 and 12, exactly the 12-electron system is a positive 4k system. The theorem proves antiaromaticCount .singletC13 = 1.
